hops.query: Export control restrictions and regulations risks affecting sales of products to customers and markets outside the United States
hops.rationale: All five passages come from NVDA accession 000104581024000029, the filing-year-2024 10-K with fiscal period ended January 28, 2024, so the filter matches. They directly address export control risks on sales outside the US: restrictions reducing demand in Europe, Latin America, and Southeast Asia; GPU controls that could bar exports to customers or markets; design-out effects; and Russia/Belarus sanctions that blocked product shipments and led to stopping direct Russia sales. Passages are truncated mid-sentence, but the substance is fully supported.

hops.query: Dependence on third-party foundries, contract manufacturers, and external manufacturing and packaging capacity supply constraints
hops.rationale: All evidence comes from the NVDA 2024 filing (accession 000104581024000029, fiscal period ended January 28, 2024). Passages 49, 50, and 41 directly address the subquery: reliance on foundries for wafers, use of independent subcontractors for assembly, test, and packaging, no guaranteed wafer or capacity supply, long lead times, supplier concentration, and manufacturing yield risk. Passage 114 adds capacity purchase commitments and long third-party lead times. Passage 58 covers third-party cybersecurity supply chain risk and is off-topic. The evidence does not address export controls, which the audit also requires, but this subquery is about manufacturing dependence and it is well supported.

Additionally, we depend on developers, customers and other third parties to build, enhance, and maintain accelerated computing applications that leverage our platforms. We also rely on third-party content providers and publishers to make their content available on our platforms, such as GeForce NOW. Failure by developers, customers, and other third parties to build, enhance, and maintain applications that leverage our platforms, or failure by third-party content providers or publishers to make their content available on reasonable terms or at all for use by our customers or end users on our platforms, could adversely affect customer demand. Dependency on third-party suppliers and their technology to manufacture, assemble, test, or package our products reduces our control over product quantity and quality, manufacturing yields, and product delivery schedules and could harm our business. We depend on foundries to manufacture our semiconductor wafers using their fabrication equipment and techniques. We do not assemble, test, or package our products, but instead contract with independent subcontractors. These subcontractors assist with procuring components used in our systems, boards, and products. We face several risks which have adversely affected or could adversely affect our ability to meet customer demand and scale our supply chain, negatively impact longer-term demand for our products and services, and adversely affect our business operations, gross margin, revenue and/or financial results, including: • lack of guaranteed supply of wafer, component and capacity or decommitment and potential higher wafer and component prices, from incorrectly estimating

Risks Related to Demand, Supply and Manufacturing Failure to estimate customer demand accurately has led and could lead to mismatches between supply and demand. We are not provided guaranteed wafer, component and capacity supply, and our supply deliveries and production may be non-linear within a quarter or year.
